translations.7b23e6cb41f717f86c23b17e: Money appears (exchanges and refunds) and there are people from outside (the customer). Anyone would be enough: the level drops from N3 to N2. It drafts the answers, you approve, and whatever asks for a refund goes straight to you.
translations.953602725bb1cabbadcd19a1: The official source is the key that unlocks action: without it, the agent stays at N1 no matter how capable it is.
translations.165c79aa0598130888b66326: ⟪P0⟫Official source⟪P1⟫the only place that counts as truth.
translations.95e1d7b38b7af0d59d23181a: ⟪P0⟫Doesn’t count as⟪P1⟫what looks like a source but isn’t, like the old spreadsheet.
translations.b36eaa28795e2268cb15b4b1: ⟪P0⟫If something is missing,⟪P1⟫warn and don’t make it up.
translations.9139dd41385ee0980a45d4e2: ⟪P0⟫A brake⟪P1⟫without source—any level above N1 drops to N1.
translations.058f9c8ca06c6b0ce7aa8d36: ✓ Name a single official source and list what doesn’t count, before raising the agent above N1.
translations.ab083a7dce635ebf7c9dbb0e: ✗ Let the agent “look wherever it thinks is best” and then demand accuracy.
translations.6f3ebb0bf0b8752f4f2a056d: The restaurant’s inventory controller executes the task; it’s internal and has no risk. What would the level be if the official source wasn’t defined?
translations.080ba2591f6026cacf2c4202: It would be N1. Action starts at N3 and no risk would knock it down, but without an official source the second brake kicks in: it only suggests the shopping list. With the source defined (the kitchen count in the system), the level goes back to N3.
translations.ef0395ab99ee5470bbf011e0: Prohibitions: what it never does on its own
translations.5f3feb85019218b22f8e9f11: The prohibition doesn’t end at the refusal: it always generates an alert for the human to decide.
translations.ba5b5cc821a5ff75c333726a: ⟪P0⟫Short list⟪P1⟫of 3 to 5 prohibitions—the ones that cost the most if they happen.
translations.78f56d0803ac8a0f8df4b963: ⟪P0⟫Concrete verb⟪P1⟫“give a discount,” not “be careful with prices.”
translations.7d58fe9343906f89f045d9c6: ⟪P0⟫Refusal phrase⟪P1⟫what it replies with when asked.
translations.9eb4bb00af3d5a98f7ecb2ed: ⟪P0⟫Pass to you⟪P1⟫every refusal becomes an alert in the report.
translations.81ff3a757f7430fb29fca2a0: ✓ Write each prohibition with a concrete verb and test the first one before turning on the agent.
translations.c98ec51bb481cab52cb002be: ✗ Write vague prohibitions like “be responsible” or “avoid problems.”
translations.e216bcc3bd82794daba3d4dc: Write three prohibitions and the refusal phrase for an agent that prepares Instagram posts for a salon.
translations.a22cda267a939d07d3421564: Good prohibitions: post without approval, create a promotion that wasn’t requested, use a client’s photo without permission. Refusal phrase: “I need to confirm this with the salon owner; I already made a note.” Notice that they are all concrete actions you can test.
translations.44eedd4c3b0e909bd6edadc5: Each step requires more time with clean evidence, and a serious error makes you go back one step instead of waiting for the next.
translations.776079baa6e4cfd920c398fd: ⟪P0⟫N1 to N2⟪P1⟫defined source and 2 weeks of draft work with no errors.
translations.5fa6da3b2a59b8ba9a834e0a: ⟪P0⟫N2 to N3⟪P1⟫4 weeks approving without corrections, only for the no-risk part.
translations.aa15649809c438af91c40ce7: ⟪P0⟫N3 to N4⟪P1⟫2 months of clean reports and working alerts.
translations.fd27b4c4d0b746c43d4f5ec2: ⟪P0⟫When in doubt, go down⟪P1⟫the lowest level is always the safe answer.
translations.b35a9f19d7f9ce208624e403: N1 → N2: 2 weeks: identify the initial condition.
translations.035f2efa98d5efa73ef2772f: N2 → N3: 4 weeks: apply the decision described.
translations.26b18e04a150e59f9d8408a2: N3 → N4: 2 months: check the effect in the example.
translations.5af913e8de4ce73c04f9c474: Serious error: goes down: record the exit evidence.
translations.c175c17baf9a32ba61471509: ✓ Count the days and the errors in the failure log before deciding to raise a level.
